title: Crispy Chicken Burgers
subtitle: thick panko-crusted chicken cutlets fried golden, on toasted buns with honey mayo, lettuce and tomato
imageAlt: A crispy golden chicken burger with lettuce and tomato on a toasted bun on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 4 big burgers: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Two chicken breasts, halved into thin cutlets, make 4 burgers that cook fast and evenly.

steps.title: Cutlets
steps.text: Slice each breast in half horizontally to make 4 cutlets. Cover with plastic wrap and pound to an even 1.5 cm thick.

steps.title: Set up
steps.text: Mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper in one shallow dish. Beat the eggs with the milk in a second, and put the panko in a third.

steps.title: Bread
steps.text: Coat each cutlet in the flour, then the egg, then press firmly into the panko on both sides.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium until a panko crumb sizzles right away. Fry 2 cutlets at a time, 4–5 minutes a side, until deep golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre. Drain on a rack.

steps.title: Sauce and buns
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, honey and lemon juice together. Toast the buns cut side down in a dry pan, 1 minute.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Spread the honey mayo on both halves of each bun, then add lettuce, a cutlet and tomato.

fixIt.fix: Pat the chicken dry before the flour, and don't move the cutlets for the first 2 minutes in the pan.
The oil was too hot or the cutlets too thick. Pound them evenly and finish in a 200°C (400°F) oven for 5 minutes if needed.
The oil wasn't hot enough. Wait until a crumb sizzles hard, and drain on a rack, not paper.

saleTip: Chicken breasts are often $8.80/kg in No Frills value packs; cut, bread and freeze extra cutlets flat.
swap: Air fryer: spray the breaded cutlets with oil and cook at 200°C, 12–14 minutes, flipping halfway, to 74°C (165°F); no frying oil needed.
leftovers: Reheat the cutlets in the oven or air fryer so they stay crisp; build the burger fresh.
doneness: Chicken cutlets at 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested crispy chicken sandwich methods (America's Test Kitchen, Food Network Canada): pounded breast cutlets, flour-egg-panko breading, shallow-fried at medium heat.
prepAhead: Bread the cutlets up to 4 hours ahead; keep uncovered on a rack in the fridge.
Freeze breaded raw cutlets flat on a tray, then bag; fry from thawed.
reheat: Cutlets on a rack at 200°C (400°F) for 10 minutes, or the air fryer at 190°C for 6–8 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

stepNotes.4: Basic: plain mayonnaise, no honey or lemon.

fancy.note: Melted cheddar and crisp bacon on every burger.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: first bake the bacon on a sheet at 200°C (400°F), 15–18 minutes, until crisp.

addSteps.title: Cheese and bacon
addSteps.text: Lay a cheddar slice on each hot cutlet as it comes out of the pan so it melts, and add a slice of bacon to each burger.

plating: Burger on the plate with a toothpick through the middle.
Cut in half to show the crunch.
Extra honey mayo in a little dish for dipping.

why.0-8: Panko's big flakes fry up crunchier and absorb less oil than fine crumbs.
why.0-7: A splash of milk thins the egg so the coating stays even and light.
why.1-1: Honey in the mayo gives that sweet-and-savoury fast-food sauce.

funFact: Panko comes from the Japanese 'pan' (bread) and 'ko' (crumb); it's made from crustless bread baked with electric current.

keeps.note: cooked cutlets only, not built burgers

pairs: the air fryer fries from the chicken tenders
